title: What the sensor cannot tell us

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Our river project installed water sensors at three locations. They record temperature every hour, giving us a much clearer picture of daily changes.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: However, a sensor reading alone cannot explain why a change happened. A warmer reading might reflect sunlight, lower water levels, or a technical fault.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Volunteers therefore visit the sites every Saturday. They photograph the area and record observations, such as recent rain or nearby construction.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Combining these notes with the measurements helps us ask better questions. We publish the raw data, but we clearly distinguish observations from conclusions.

questions.explanation: The measurements are hourly.
questions.evidence: They record temperature every hour

questions.prompt: Why are sensor readings alone insufficient?
options: They do not explain the cause of a change.
answers: They do not explain the cause of a change.
questions.explanation: Several different causes could explain one reading.
questions.evidence: a sensor reading alone cannot explain why a change happened

questions.explanation: Visits happen weekly on Saturday.
questions.evidence: visit the sites every Saturday

questions.prompt: What does the project distinguish in its reports?
questions.explanation: The presenter emphasizes careful interpretation.
questions.evidence: we clearly distinguish observations from conclusions

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: You used to spend more time planning your study than actually studying. What changed?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: I stopped trying to design a perfect timetable. Now I choose one small task each evening and connect it to something I already do, like making tea.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: How do you know whether the method is working?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Every Sunday, I review an old recording or draft. I look for one improvement and one thing to practice next. I don't expect progress to be identical every week.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: So consistency matters more than a complicated system?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: For me, yes. A plan should make starting easier. If it becomes another task to avoid, it needs to be simpler.

questions.prompt: What was the guest's earlier problem?
options: Too much planning and too little practice
answers: Too much planning and too little practice
questions.explanation: The host describes the imbalance.
questions.evidence: more time planning your study than actually studying

questions.prompt: The guest connects study to a habit such as making ____.
questions.explanation: Tea-making is the example of an existing routine.
questions.evidence: like making tea

questions.explanation: The guest reviews weekly.
questions.evidence: Every Sunday, I review an old recording or draft.

questions.prompt: What should a good plan do, according to the guest?
questions.explanation: A useful plan reduces the difficulty of beginning.
questions.evidence: A plan should make starting easier.
